prompt:
[REFERENCE CONTROL]

Use the uploaded Part 1 storyboard image as the PRIMARY visual and narrative reference for the entire video.

Use it to preserve:
- exact story progression
- Lena Cruz and Jax Mercer character identity
- wardrobe and bandana colors
- gas-station environment
- cashier appearance
- paper bag and “TOO SLOW.” note
- black drive design
- black SUV convoy
- dark muscle car
- sunset color palette
- cinematic graphic-novel visual language
- suspense-to-action escalation
- Part 1 cliffhanger ending

Do NOT reproduce the storyboard sheet itself in the finished video.
No panel borders, timestamps, handwritten captions, production notes, reference-sheet layout, paper texture, storyboard numbering, or storyboard text should appear in the video.

Transform the storyboard into one continuous polished cinematic animated action sequence.

[VIDEO GOAL]

Duration: exactly 15 seconds
Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape
Style: premium cinematic 2D graphic-novel animation
Genre: action thriller / crime chase
Tone: stylish, tense, fast, mysterious, controlled
Story structure:
quiet pickup → suspicious exchange → betrayal reveal → convoy trap → rapid escape → real drive spotted → chase begins

This is PART 1 only.

Do NOT continue into the highway chase or overpass confrontation.
The exact final story beat is Lena realizing:
“They still have it.”

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK]

LENA CRUZ:
Young athletic woman with a high dark ponytail, sharp expressive eyes, red patterned bandana covering or resting around her lower face, fitted dark cropped top, light denim shorts, practical shoes, lean athletic proportions.

Personality:
bold, observant, quick-reacting, fearless, direct.

Beginning emotional state:
controlled suspicion.

Ending emotional state:
focused determination.

Keep identical throughout:
- facial structure
- skin tone
- ponytail
- red bandana
- dark cropped top
- denim shorts
- body proportions
- age
- eye shape
- silhouette

Do not change her hairstyle, outfit, facial proportions, or bandana pattern.

JAX MERCER:
Tall athletic young man with short dark hair, intense eyes, blue/dark patterned bandana covering his lower face, fitted dark charcoal T-shirt, brown/dark pants, strong controlled proportions.

Personality:
calm, tactical, observant, protective, efficient.

Beginning emotional state:
quiet vigilance.

Ending emotional state:
focused pursuit mode.

Keep identical throughout:
- face
- short dark hairstyle
- blue bandana
- charcoal shirt
- dark pants
- build
- height
- proportions

CASHIER:
Ordinary nervous convenience-store employee.
Dark slightly messy hair, worried expression, simple work clothes.
He is frightened and uncomfortable, not villainous.

RICO’S CREW:
Mostly seen through silhouettes, vehicle interiors, distant figures and brief readable glimpses.
Dark streetwear.
No unnecessary close-ups or extra character identities.

[KEY PROP LOCK]

BLACK DRIVE:
Small matte-black rectangular data device.
Simple clean shape.
The REAL black drive is NOT inside the paper bag.
It is seen clearly later in the hand of Rico’s crew near the lead SUV.

FAKE PACKAGE:
Plain brown paper bag.

Inside:
- cheap small green novelty keychain
- folded paper note

The note must clearly communicate:
“TOO SLOW.”

Do not introduce additional items.

MUSCLE CAR:
Dark charcoal/black classic-inspired muscle car.
Wide aggressive stance.
Warm red rear lights.
No logos or recognizable real-world branding.

BLACK SUVs:
Large dark SUVs with bright headlights.
Consistent model and silhouette throughout the video.
No brand badges.

[WORLD / PHYSICS RULES]

The action follows realistic cinematic cause-and-effect.

Every movement must have:
anticipation → action → physical consequence → reaction.

Examples:
- headlights appear → Jax notices → body turns → he warns Lena
- Lena realizes trap → immediately creates cover
- Jax identifies escape route → forces open rear exit
- they reach car → Lena spots black drive → Jax accelerates

No random explosions.
No supernatural movement.
No teleporting.
No impossible weapon behavior.
No excessive debris.

Keep action grounded, readable, and fast.

integrated_multimodal_description:

[SHOT 1] (0.00s–2.20s) — THE PICKUP

Start with a wide cinematic exterior of the isolated roadside gas station under a dramatic orange-magenta sunset.

Long shadows cross slightly wet asphalt.
The convenience-store interior glows with cool fluorescent light.
The station canopy is illuminated against the colorful dusk sky.

Lena and Jax walk toward the station together from the foreground.

As they approach the pumps, they stop.

Jax slowly scans the perimeter, checking parked vehicles, road entrances, and reflections in the store windows.

Lena adjusts the red bandana over her lower face and looks toward the convenience-store door.

She gives Jax a tiny confirming glance.

Jax gives a subtle nod.

Lena separates from him and walks toward the store.

Camera:
Begin with a low wide-angle establishing dolly toward them.
Transition into a medium two-shot.
Subtle arc around Lena as she turns toward the entrance.

Emotion:
quiet professionalism with underlying suspicion.

Dialogue:

Jax (low controlled voice):
<d>[English] Two minutes. If anything feels wrong, walk.</d>

Lena (dry, confident):
<d>[English] You worry too much.</d>

Jax:
<d>[English] That’s why we’re still alive.</d>

Sound:
- distant highway ambience
- light desert wind
- faint fuel-pump hum
- shoes on asphalt
- distant car pass
- soft fabric movement
- subtle atmospheric thriller pulse begins

Transition:
Follow Lena through the glass entrance.

[SHOT 2] (2.20s–4.40s) — THE HANDOFF

Inside the convenience store.

The lighting shifts from warm sunset orange outside to cool desaturated fluorescent interior light.

Lena walks toward the counter.

The cashier watches her nervously.

His eyes briefly flick toward the front windows before returning to Lena.

Lena notices this.

The cashier slowly slides a plain brown paper bag across the counter.

Lena does not immediately grab it.

She studies the cashier.

He avoids eye contact.

Then Lena takes the bag.

Camera:
Medium tracking shot behind Lena entering the store.
Cut to cashier’s anxious close-up.
Insert close-up of the brown paper bag sliding across the counter.
Slow push toward Lena’s eyes.

Emotion:
suspicion increasing.

Dialogue:

Lena (quiet):
<d>[English] Where’s Vale?</d>

Cashier (nervous, whispering):
<d>[English] I... I was only told to give you the bag.</d>

Lena:
<d>[English] Told by who?</d>

The cashier says nothing.

Sound:
- fluorescent electrical hum
- refrigerator compressor
- paper bag scraping across countertop
- subtle nervous breath from cashier
- distant exterior traffic

Music:
Minimal low electronic pulse, restrained.

Transition:
Lena opens the bag.

[SHOT 3] (4.40s–6.20s) — TOO SLOW

Tight insert inside the paper bag.

Instead of the black drive:
a cheap green novelty keychain and folded paper note.

Lena pulls out the note.

She unfolds it.

The message reads:
“TOO SLOW.”

Hold just long enough to understand.

Cut to extreme close-up of Lena’s eyes above the red bandana.

Her expression immediately changes from suspicion to certainty.

She looks toward the front windows.

Camera:
Macro insert inside bag.
Match cut from unfolded paper to Lena’s eyes.
Very slow push-in.

Emotion:
realization.

Dialogue:

Lena (under her breath):
<d>[English] Damn it.</d>

Cashier (frightened):
<d>[English] I’m sorry.</d>

Sound:
- paper unfolding
- subtle bass hit when message is revealed
- refrigerator hum suddenly feels louder
- tiny room-tone drop immediately before Lena reacts

Transition:
Hard motivated cut from Lena’s eyes to bright headlights outside.

[SHOT 4] (6.20s–8.40s) — THE TRAP CLOSES

Exterior from Jax’s perspective.

Multiple black SUVs turn into the gas station from different entrances.

Headlights flare directly toward him.

One SUV swings across the driveway.
Another rolls near the pumps.
A third blocks the road exit.

Jax instantly understands.

His relaxed posture snaps into tactical alertness.

He turns toward the convenience store.

Camera:
Over-the-shoulder behind Jax facing approaching SUVs.
Fast controlled push-in as headlights appear.
Brief low-angle shot of tires turning into the station.
Return to Jax.

Dialogue:

Jax (sharp, loud):
<d>[English] Lena! Move!</d>

Inside, Lena immediately turns toward his voice.

Lena:
<d>[English] I knew it.</d>

Sound:
- SUV engines approaching
- tire grit
- doors beginning to open
- Jax’s shout
- store door bell rattling
- thriller percussion enters

Transition:
Cut on Lena’s rapid turn.

[SHOT 5] (8.40s–10.80s) — BREAK THE TRAP

Inside the store, Lena reacts instantly.

She grabs the edge of a lightweight product display and shoves it sideways, creating visual cover between herself and the front windows.

Packaged goods scatter across the floor.

No one is struck.

At the same time outside, Jax moves along the side of the building toward a rear service exit.

He shoulders or kicks the jammed rear door near the latch.

The door bursts outward.

Use a rapid intercut rhythm between Lena and Jax.

Lena sprints toward the rear.

Jax reaches through and pulls the door wide for her.

Camera:
Dynamic medium tracking with Lena.
Low angle as display moves.
Cut to Jax moving beside brick wall.
Close shot on his boot/body impacting the jammed door.
Wide rear-exit reveal.

Emotion:
rapid controlled survival response.

Dialogue:

Jax:
<d>[English] Back exit! Go!</d>

Lena:
<d>[English] Moving!</d>

Sound:
- shelves rattling
- packaged items falling
- shoe impacts
- rear-door metal thud
- alarm begins chirping
- SUV doors outside
- tense rhythmic percussion increasing

No gunfire is necessary.
The threat should come from the trap and incoming crew, not graphic violence.

Transition:
Lena bursts through the rear door past Jax.

[SHOT 6] (10.80s–12.80s) — RUN FOR THE CAR

Lena and Jax sprint together behind the station.

Industrial rear lot:
chain-link fence,
service barrels,
wet asphalt,
dumpsters,
utility pipes,
warm sunset beyond the rooftops.

Alarm light flashes intermittently across the walls.

Their dark muscle car is parked ahead.

Jax runs slightly toward the driver side.
Lena heads toward passenger side.

Camera:
Low side tracking shot moving parallel with them.
Brief rear tracking shot toward the car.
Natural speed blur at frame edges while keeping faces and silhouettes readable.

Dialogue:

Lena (breathing hard):
<d>[English] Tell me you brought the car.</d>

Jax:
<d>[English] You’re looking at it.</d>

Lena:
<d>[English] Good answer.</d>

Sound:
- fast footsteps
- breathing
- clothing movement
- alarm chirp
- distant SUV engines
- keys / car unlock click

Transition:
As Lena reaches the passenger door, something behind them catches her eye.

[SHOT 7] (12.80s–15.00s) — THE REAL DRIVE / CLIFFHANGER

Lena glances backward.

Across the rear service lot, one of Rico’s crew is stepping into the lead black SUV.

In his hand:
the REAL matte-black drive.

Make the black drive clearly visible for a brief readable moment against the sunset/headlight contrast.

Lena’s eyes lock onto it.

Jax is already in the driver seat and starts the muscle car.

Lena dives into the passenger side.

The engine roars.

The lead SUV accelerates away.

Jax launches after it.

The muscle car swings out from behind the station and begins pursuit as other black SUVs move behind them.

Finish with a powerful rear three-quarter chase composition:
muscle car accelerating into the sunset,
red taillights glowing,
black SUVs ahead and behind,
dust and road grit lifting.

Include a brief insert of Lena’s determined eyes reflected in the side mirror.

Dialogue:

Lena (urgent):
<d>[English] Jax—the drive!</d>

Jax:
<d>[English] I see it.</d>

Lena:
<d>[English] They still have it.</d>

Jax (calm):
<d>[English] Then we take it back.</d>

Sound:
- car ignition
- deep engine rev
- door slam
- tire chirp
- accelerating muscle-car engine
- SUV engines
- gravel scattering
- wind building
- final rising cinematic pulse

End exactly as the pursuit begins.

Do NOT show the highway chase beyond the first acceleration.

audio_description:

Create native synchronized cinematic stereo audio.

ENVIRONMENT:
- desert-edge evening wind
- distant highway traffic
- fuel-pump hum
- convenience-store fluorescent buzz
- refrigeration units
- rear service-lot ambience

FOLEY:
- bandana fabric
- footsteps
- paper bag movement
- note unfolding
- product rack sliding
- loose packages falling
- metal rear door impact
- clothing movement during sprint
- vehicle doors
- ignition
- tires
- engine acceleration

CHARACTER VOICES:

Lena:
young adult woman,
calm but assertive,
slightly dry confidence,
controlled breathing during action,
never screaming unnecessarily.

Jax:
young adult man,
low calm tactical voice,
economical delivery,
becomes sharper only when warning Lena.

Cashier:
young adult male,
quiet,
nervous,
breathy,
clearly frightened by the situation.

Do not give dialogue to Rico’s crew in this clip.

non_diegetic_music:

Start with restrained cinematic synth pulse and low atmospheric bass.

0.00–4.40:
minimal tension pulse.

4.40–6.20:
low bass accent when “TOO SLOW.” is revealed.

6.20–10.80:
introduce restrained percussion and faster pulse as SUVs arrive.

10.80–12.80:
increase rhythm during the escape sprint.

12.80–15.00:
short rising action motif synchronized with ignition and acceleration.

Music must remain beneath dialogue and sound effects.

Do NOT make the soundtrack heroic yet.
Part 1 should end unresolved.

[VISUAL STYLE]

Premium cinematic 2D graphic-novel animation.

Visual qualities:
- refined ink outlines
- painterly cel shading
- subtle paper-brush texture inside artwork
- realistic but stylized anatomy
- strong silhouettes
- expressive eyes
- controlled motion blur
- cinematic color grading
- dramatic sunset rim lighting
- high environment detail
- atmospheric reflections
- restrained depth of field
- polished film-like compositing

Palette:
- burnt sunset orange
- dusty magenta
- violet-purple sky
- teal/cyan fluorescent interior
- charcoal vehicles
- asphalt gray
- red taillights
- cool blue shadows

Do not make the finished video look like a paper storyboard.
It should look like a completed animated graphic-novel action film.

[CAMERA LANGUAGE]

Use intentional cinematic camera movements:

- slow dolly during initial approach
- controlled push-ins for suspicion
- macro insert for package reveal
- over-the-shoulder convoy reveal
- fast but readable tracking for escape
- low-angle running shots
- brief handheld-like urgency during trap reveal, but still smooth and readable
- rear three-quarter vehicle shot for cliffhanger

Camera should become progressively more energetic:

calm → suspicious → compressed → urgent → fast.

Do not use:
- random spinning
- excessive Dutch angles
- chaotic handheld shake
- meaningless zooms
- unreadable fast cutting

[MOTION RULES]

Character movement must feel physically grounded.

Lena:
quick decisive reactions,
athletic acceleration,
sharp head turns,
efficient body movement.

Jax:
controlled economy of motion,
fast tactical reactions,
strong purposeful running.

Vehicles:
realistic mass,
suspension response,
tire grip,
acceleration,
headlight movement,
no weightless drifting.

Cloth:
bandanas and ponytail react naturally to running and wind.

Objects:
paper, packages, doors, and displays obey physical momentum.

[CONTINUITY RULES]

Keep all identities identical across every shot.

Lena:
same face,
same ponytail,
same red bandana,
same top,
same shorts.

Jax:
same face,
same short dark hair,
same blue/dark bandana,
same shirt,
same pants.

Cashier:
same appearance during all store shots.

Muscle car:
same body design and color.

SUVs:
same consistent dark design.

Black drive:
same small matte-black rectangular object.

Keep spatial geography coherent:
front gas station → convenience-store interior → side/rear exit → rear parking lot → muscle car → road.

Do not teleport characters between locations.

Do not show Rico clearly in Part 1.

[SAFETY / NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS]

Keep action stylized, cinematic, and non-graphic.

No blood.
No gore.
No visible wounds.
No executions.
No graphic impacts.
No cruelty.
No civilians harmed.
No cashier harmed.
No explosive destruction.
No graphic weapon discharge.
No threatening close-up gun violence.

No storyboard sheet visible.
No panel borders.
No captions.
No timestamps.
No title cards.
No production notes.
No subtitles.
No logos.
No watermarks.
No real brands.
No readable store branding.
No recognizable copyrighted characters.
No random text except the intentional physical handwritten note “TOO SLOW.”
No identity drift.
No duplicate Lena.
No duplicate Jax.
No changing costumes.
No changing vehicle designs.
No extra limbs.
No malformed hands.
No distorted faces.
No disappearing bandanas.
No random props.
No scene confusion.
No hyperreal live action.
No 3D game-render look.
No anime-style transformation.

FINAL FRAME:
The muscle car accelerates after the escaping SUV convoy beneath the burning sunset.
Lena’s determined eyes briefly visible in the mirror.
The line “They still have it” has just been spoken.
The chase has begun.

CUT TO BLACK.
